what: Every BILLS package in the 2026-09-19 text-versions census sample (docs/research/billtrax-raw-data-2026-09-19.json) that offers a United States Legislative Markup rendition, with that rendition fetched through GovInfoBodyAcquirer.acquire(package, prefer=('uslm',)) -- keyed summary, keyed MODS, keyless body -- and its text derived through extraction.body_text.body_text, exactly as a caller would.

census_reconciliation.census_sample: sources.textVersionsVocabulary pins 24 version codes, each to one representative sample file; the run's own formatTypeCounts aggregate sums to 240 format entries with 10 United States Legislative Markup.
census_reconciliation.correction: The 240/10 aggregate counts each sampled bill once per version code that pinned it: hconres11 is the sample for both enr and rds, hres1274 for eh and rh, hr3426 for eh1s, rfs2 and rhuc. Re-deriving the 20 distinct bills' full version histories (receipt 01_discovery_result.json, 20 keyed Congress.gov /text requests) gives 61 versions and 188 distinct format entries, 9 of them USLM; hconres11's single USLM entry counted twice is the whole of the census's 10. Of the 9 distinct entries, 4 are the 'Public Law' version on a bill's /text endpoint -- PLAW-collection packages (PLAW-119publN_uslm.xml), which sources/govinfo/uslm.py's own grammar already reads and which the BILLS package grammar this gap closes does not cover. In scope: the 5 BILLS enrolled packages below.
